name: Герои за золото, партия 1: десять героев каталога золота цикла II (c2-01…c2-10: Гримса Гудок, Ансельм Девятый, Бастиан Ольт, Бьорн Станина, Трюд Настойщица, Фрида Рудная Пыль, Вигдис Щебень, Эльдгрим Молот, Скегги Огнестрел, Ньяль Рудный Меняла). Решение автора 30.09.2026: портреты героев за золото рисуем постепенно, партиями по 10, после каждой автор смотрит результат. Рецепт — принятые jobs/heroes-batch-05.json и heroes-batch-04.json: тот же стиль, запреты, три референса стиля, рамка (кадр по пояс, корпус вправо, к врагам, камера чуть снизу, нижний край режет фигуру по поясу, низ плавно уходит в тень без плашки и надписей); способ «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md): кто он и чего хочет сейчас · характер телом · поза словами в миг действия · пять личных деталей из «кто он» и главы · место. Опора под ногами в промт не пишется (урок первой партии). Дворфов называем пропорциями; дворфийки без бороды, как принятые c2-41 и c4-45. Источники: design/ui/roster.js (who, ch) — главы docs/content/герои/главы/цикл-2.md; место — свод лора (docs/lore/свод-лора-текст.txt, «Стоун-Хейм»): гора-отшельник Кароксорр в опасных землях, одни узкие ворота, машины на станинах, гильдейские дружины с огнестрелом и молотами; внутри — полость, город ярусами-уступами, мосты, виадуки, клети подъёмников, литейные с рыжим огнём; ночи нет — смены по гудку; Библиотека — светлая колоннада под сводом, куда не пускают дым. Тварей от ручьёв не рисуем — только угроза за правым краем. Редкость не рисуем, класс — по оружию или действию, школа — по цвету света; у героев без стихии (Трюд, Ньяль) свет — лампы и фонари. Детали, которых нет в главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no writing on paper, books, maps or stones, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no name plate, no dark band at the bottom, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood, no monsters in the picture. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes.

heroes.frame: Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the belt or the hips; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame, whatever the pose. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression. The lower part of the picture sinks gradually into deeper shadow — no band, no plate, nothing written. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

jobs.subject: Subject: Grimsa the Shift-Horn, a dwarf woman of the great city inside the dwarven mountain, a controller of the Earth school who stops her foes in their tracks. Who she is: inside the mountain there is no sun and no night — the horn of the shifts replaces them, and for sixty years it was she who gave it, in three voices: shift, meal, shift. By her horn the mountain worked, was born and died, and not once was it late. To the young who went down to the deepest tunnels she said one thing: breathe slowly and count, like the miner who breathed under the rubble for five days. Right now she hauls the lever, and the voice of the mountain strikes the enemy. Character: exact, stern and indomitable — the voice the whole mountain lives by; her jaw set, her heavy brows drawn together, her deep-set eyes fixed on the enemy, her chest full of a slow, counted breath. She is unmistakably a dwarf: short and enormously broad, a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; she has no beard — her chin and upper lip are bare, warm living skin. An old dwarf woman in her eighties, a weathered ruddy face, snow-white hair in two heavy braids wound around her head. Pose, the moment of the horn: the camera is low; she is turned toward the right, braced, her whole weight thrown into the pull. She has exactly two arms: her far hand hauls down a long iron lever with all her weight; her near hand is flung out toward the right, pointing, and the roaring voice of the horn rolls toward the enemy beyond the right edge as a great ring of amber-orange light of the Earth school, rippling the air and scattering steam and dust. Details that tell her story: (1) above her, the horn itself: three brass whistles of different sizes on one thick pipe — three voices — blasting white steam; (2) the wooden grip of the lever is worn smooth and pale by sixty years of her hand; (3) a big shift hourglass in a brass frame stands on the ledge beside her, its sand running; (4) a leather cap with thick felt ear-flaps turned up; (5) a heavy leather coat with brass buttons, damp with steam and streaked with soot. Place: a small iron platform high on the wall of a vast cavern inside the dwarven mountain: the city climbs the cavern walls in tiers and ledges, with bridges, rail viaducts and lift cages hanging on chains over the dark depths; the orange fire of foundries glows far below; steam everywhere, a stone vault overhead instead of a sky. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the wave of the horn and from the cracks below; the orange glow of the foundries in the depths.

jobs.subject: Subject: Anselm the Ninth, a man of the great white-stone harbor city of the west, a battle mage of the Water school. Who he is: a scribe who wanted to read inside the dwarven mountain, where knowledge is gathered, not hidden. Nine times he brought lists of laws, maps, recipes and poems to the gate of the dwarves' great Library, and nine times the gatekeeper told him they had that already. Then he sat down at the gate and wrote down what the mountain already knew, traced from the refusals like prints; they had no such inventory, and the tenth time he was let in. Right now, on the upper tier of the Library, he strikes at the one who would take the book from his hands. Character: patient, stubborn and quietly fierce — a man refused nine times who came back a tenth; his lean face set, his thin lips pressed in a stubborn line, his eyes bright with a scholar's hunger and burning with anger. A lean man in his fifties with a sharp, clever face, dark hair going grey at the temples tied back, and a short neat beard. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; he is turned toward the right, stepping forward. He has exactly two arms: his near hand is thrust toward the right, and a roaring torrent of blue water-light of the Water school bursts from his palm and twists like a spear toward the enemy beyond the right edge; his far arm holds a thick old book against his chest, closed over one finger to keep his page. Details that tell his story: (1) the book is bound in worn brown leather with brass corners — he has not finished reading it; (2) his fingers and cuffs are stained with ink; (3) a scribe's brass writing case and a stoppered inkwell hang at his belt; (4) a leather satchel over his shoulder is stuffed with rolled papers tied with cord, nothing written visible — the knowledge he brought nine times; (5) a long travelling coat of dark blue wool, worn and dusty from nine journeys. Place: the upper tier of the dwarven Library right under the vault of a vast cavern: a long, bright colonnade of pale stone where no smoke is let in; glass showcases holding strange mechanisms, foreign weapons and rolled scrolls; beyond the balustrade, far below, the tiers of a city inside the mountain glowing with orange foundry fires. Cool blue light of the Water school rises from the torrent and from below; the calm pale light of the colonnade.

jobs.subject: Subject: Bastian Olt, a man of the west, a swift hunter of the Air school. Who he is: a hunter hired by the keeper of the dwarven Library's showcases for a single season — to catch a grey she-beast alive. He had taken bigger beasts; after the season he extended the contract at his own expense, because the grey one led him in circles over the stones and each time turned up behind his back, watching. He began to understand that he was being studied too. Right now he lunges at his quarry — and behind him, high on a rock, the grey one watches. Character: proud, dogged and quick — a professional who hates to lose; his teeth bared in a hard grin, his eyes sharp and narrowed on the target, and a flicker of unease on his brow, as if he feels eyes on his back. A lean, weathered man in his thirties with a sunburnt face, stubble, brown hair tied back and a scar through one eyebrow. Pose, the moment of the lunge: the camera is low; he lunges forward toward the right, low and fast, his weight thrown forward. He has exactly two arms: his near hand grips a light hunting spear far forward on the shaft, thrusting it toward the right; his far hand drives the butt of the spear; a spiral of pale white-green wind of the Air school runs along the shaft to the point. Details that tell his story: (1) a hunting net weighted with small stones is coiled over his shoulder, tufts of grey fur caught in its cords; (2) a necklace of big fangs and claws — trophies of larger beasts; (3) a frayed and patched hunter's cloak of grey-brown wool — a second season paid from his own purse; (4) a long hunting knife in a worn sheath at his belt; (5) high on a rock behind him, small and in soft focus, a great grey lynx with long black ear tufts sits and watches him with calm pale-gold eyes. Place: a grey stony wasteland at the foot of a lone, enormous mountain at rainy dusk: boulders and scree, small stones sliding down the slope, low clouds. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the wet stones below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Bjorn Bedframe, a dwarf of the guild guard, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: the gate of the dwarven mountain is narrow on purpose — it holds one war machine on its iron bed and one dwarf. For forty years that dwarf was he. The machine strikes while it has fuel, he stands while he can stand — that was how they shared the work. Right now the machine beside him has fired until it burnt out dry and fallen silent, and he holds the gap alone with his shield until the shift horn: to leave the post before the relief comes is a disgrace. Character: stolid, dutiful and unbreakable — a dwarf who counts in shifts; his teeth bared under the beard with the strain, his brows lowered, his eyes calm and fixed on the enemy beyond the right edge. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide, once-broken nose; in his sixties, a black beard shot with grey in two thick braids bound with iron rings. He is fully armoured, no bare skin but his face and hands: a heavy coat of overlapping iron scales over thick leather, broad iron pauldrons, leather sleeves and iron vambraces, a leather cap bound with iron bands. Pose, the moment of holding: the camera is low; he throws his whole body behind his shield like a battering ram, turned toward the right, leaning hard into it, his shoulder pressed into its back. He has exactly two arms: his near arm drives a tall, heavy rectangular shield of riveted iron forward toward the right against a blow; his far hand grips the upper rim of the shield, holding it steady. The shield takes a blow from the right: sparks and stone dust burst from its face, and amber-orange light of the Earth school bursts from the cracked stone under the impact. Details that tell his story: (1) right beside him stands the war machine, silent: a squat, heavy dwarven engine of blackened iron and brass with a short thick barrel, mounted on a massive riveted iron bed-frame; it is burnt out, its barrel glowing dull red, thin smoke curling from it; (2) his shield is dented and patched with riveted plates over and over — forty years at the gate; (3) the guild guard's scale armour, scratched and blackened; (4) the gateway is a narrow passage of rough-hewn dark stone blocks, plain, with no carving and no ornament, closing in on both sides — room only for the machine and one dwarf; (5) sweat and soot streak his face — he has stood for hours. Place: the narrow gate of a lone dwarven mountain at dusk: plain rough stone walls close on both sides, heavy iron doors deep behind him, a dim, dusty wasteland beyond. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the cracks below; the dull red glow of the spent machine.

jobs.subject: Subject: Trud the Tincture-Keeper, a dwarf woman of the great city inside the dwarven mountain, a healer. Who she is: the elves bring tinctures for burns, broken bones and poisoning into the mountain, and she knew which one was for what; she gave the miners one per shift, and more only when the alarm horn sounded. In forty years it sounded three times. The third time she went down to a collapse with a full box and gave the tinctures out without counting — for the first time in her life. The bad air below takes the healer too. Right now she holds out a tincture to a miner trapped under the rubble. Character: strict, sparing and exact all her life — and now, for the first time, generous, fierce and tender at once; her eyes watering in the bad air, her face pale and damp, but her hand perfectly steady. She is unmistakably a dwarf: short and enormously broad, a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; she has no beard — her chin and upper lip are bare, warm living skin. In her sixties, a broad round face pale under the dust, dark-brown hair streaked with grey in two thick braids under a kerchief. Pose, the moment of healing: the camera is low; she leans forward toward the right, reaching out. She has exactly two arms: her near hand holds out a small uncorked glass vial toward the wounded miner beyond the right edge, and the tincture inside glows with a soft warm light that falls on her face; her far arm clasps an open wooden box of vials against her hip. Details that tell her story: (1) the box is packed with straw and small glass vials whose tinctures glow faintly in different colours — amber, green, rose — each for its own harm; half the slots are already empty; (2) the vials are stoppered with wax and tied with plain string tags, nothing written; (3) a wet linen cloth hangs loose around her neck, pulled down from her mouth; (4) a miner's lamp hangs low from her belt and lights her face from below; (5) a leather apron over a work dress, the sleeves rolled up over strong forearms. Place: a deep mine tunnel after a collapse: broken timber props, heaps of rubble, dust and a yellowish haze of bad air hanging in the lamplight. Warm light rises from her lamp and her vials below; cold darkness beyond.

jobs.subject: Subject: Frida Ore-Dust, a dwarf woman of the great dwarven mountain, a controller of the Earth school who cripples her foes. Who she is: she sorted ore in the upper yard, and by the colour of the dust she knew which ore gives metal and which eats the lungs. Once beasts came up from the streams toward the road while a convoy stood unloaded; she slit open a sack of the most vicious dust and flung it at them, downwind — they were blinded and choking before the guard could unsling their guns. Right now she flings that dust. Character: sharp-eyed, blunt and hard as ore; her eyes narrowed against the wind, her mouth shut tight — she is holding her breath. She is unmistakably a dwarf: short and enormously broad, a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; she has no beard — her chin and upper lip are bare, warm living skin. In her sixties, a broad weathered face, iron-grey hair in tight braids pinned up; her face and hands are powdered with ore dust of many colours. Pose, the moment of the throw: the camera is low; she twists her whole body toward the right, swinging with both arms. She has exactly two arms: her near hand grips the bottom corner of a heavy slit-open sack and swings it forward toward the right in a wide arc; her far hand holds the neck of the same sack together with the short sorting knife she slit it with. Out of the long slit in the sack a great glittering cloud of rust-red and ochre ore dust flies away from her in a long arc toward the right and streams on the wind toward the enemy beyond the right edge, lit from within by amber-orange light of the Earth school. The sack is in her hands; the dust flies away from her, not onto the ground. Details that tell her story: (1) a leather sorting apron with many small pockets holding ore samples of different colours; (2) her knuckles and nails are stained with the colours of ore; (3) a dust cloth hangs loose around her neck; (4) the sorting tables behind her, with ore laid out in neat heaps by colour; (5) convoy wagons standing unloaded on the road behind her, blurred. Nothing stands in front of her. Place: the upper ore yard at the foot of a lone dwarven mountain by the road at windy dusk: sorting tables, heaps of ore, sacks, wagons, the great gate of the mountain far off. Amber-orange light of the Earth school glows inside the dust cloud and rises from the cracks in the yard below; cold blue dusk above.

jobs.title: Вигдис Щебень — дворфийка, маг ДД, Земля (c2-07, золото №7, обычная)
jobs.source: roster.js c2-07: «Маг Земли с бедного нижнего уступа. Била камнем там, где у гильдейской дружины кончались заряды»; глава «Щебень» (камень слушался раньше кирки; маги Земли — «выбравшие странное»; камня гильдия не выделяла — колдовала собой, своими годами; в последней вылазке подняла со склона всё и отдала последний год, не торгуясь). Свод: магию без посредника оплачивают годами. Решение агента: миг — поднимает весь склон, вихрь щебня и валунов летит вправо, в трещинах камней янтарь Земли; лицо молодое, а в чёрных косах седые пряди и морщинки у глаз — цена колдовства; без посоха и кристалла; кирка за спиной; залатанная куртка рудокопа не по размеру; стрелки дружины с пустыми огнестрелами в расфокусе. Дворфийка без бороды. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-07-vigdis__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-07.jpg
jobs.subject: Subject: Vigdis Rubble, a dwarf woman from the poor lower ledges of the great city inside the dwarven mountain, a battle mage of the Earth school. Who she is: on her ledge the stone obeyed her before the pick did, and the guild wrote her down among the mages — those who chose something strange, as the dwarves say. The locks of the workshops and the seals on the blueprints went to more important mages, and she went to the gate with the guild guard: where the gunners' charges ran out, her rubble began. The guild gave her no stone; she paid with herself, with her own years, and nobody counted them but her. Right now every charge has run out at once, and she raises the whole slope. Character: fierce, proud and unbargaining — when the price is named, a dwarf does not haggle; her jaw set, her eyes blazing with amber light, a defiant half-smile. She is unmistakably a dwarf: short and enormously broad, a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; she has no beard — her chin and upper lip are bare, warm living skin. Her face is young, in her thirties, but her black braids are streaked with grey and fine lines spread from the corners of her eyes — the years her magic has taken. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she is turned toward the right, both arms raised. She has exactly two arms: her near hand is thrust toward the right, fingers spread, hurling a storm of stones at the enemy beyond the right edge; her far hand is raised high above her head, palm up, lifting the slope — rubble, stones and boulders torn from the ground whirl up around her and fly toward the right, amber-orange light of the Earth school glowing in the cracks of every stone. Details that tell her story: (1) no staff and no crystal — she casts with her bare, calloused hands; (2) a miner's pick slung across her back — she was a miner first; (3) a patched, too-big leather miner's jacket from the lower ledges; (4) the grey streaks in her young braids; (5) behind her, blurred, dwarf gunners lower their empty guns. Place: a steep slope of scree and boulders below the narrow gate of a lone dwarven mountain at dusk, dust in the air. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the torn ground below; cold blue dusk above.

jobs.title: Эльдгрим Молот — дворф, физ ДД силы, Земля (c2-08, золото №8, обычная)
jobs.source: roster.js c2-08: «Молотобоец гильдейской дружины. Бил тварей у ворот тем же молотом, которым днём ковал петли для этих ворот»; глава «Петли ворот» («вещь, которую сделал сам, защищаешь сам»; тварь сорвала верхнюю петлю — забил новый штырь тем же молотом под ударами, ровно, как в кузне; остался по ту сторону створки). Решение агента: миг удара — кузнечная кувалда по дуге вправо, из бойка искры и янтарь Земли; за спиной — створка ворот на огромных кованых петлях его работы, верхняя со свежим штырём, ещё красным от жара; кожаный фартук поверх кольчуги; запасные штыри за поясом. Тварей не рисуем. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-08-eldgrim__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-08.jpg
jobs.subject: Subject: Eldgrim Hammer, a dwarf smith of the guild guard, a warrior of great strength of the Earth school. Who he is: by day he forged the hinges for the gate of the dwarven mountain, and when beasts came up from the streams he took the same hammer and went to the gate: a thing you made yourself you defend yourself. Once a beast struck the gate so hard that it tore away the upper hinge; he went outside and drove in a new pin with the same hammer, under the blows, evenly, as at the forge. The gate was closed, and he stayed on the other side. Right now he stands outside the gate and strikes. Character: calm, exact and unstoppable — a craftsman who works under blows as evenly as at his anvil; his brows lowered in concentration, his jaw clenched, his eyes narrowed on the target; he is not angry, he is working. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; in his forties, a shaved head, a thick chestnut beard in two braids singed at the ends, massive scarred forearms. Pose, the moment of the blow: the camera is low; he swings a heavy smith's sledgehammer in a great arc from over his far shoulder down toward the right, his torso twisting into the blow, all his weight behind it. He has exactly two arms: both hands grip the long hammer handle — the near hand high near the head, the far hand at the end of the handle. Sparks and amber-orange light of the Earth school burst from the hammer head. Details that tell his story: (1) the face of the hammer is polished bright by thousands of blows on the anvil; (2) a scorched smith's leather apron over a short mail shirt — forge and war at once; (3) burn scars and forge soot on his forearms; (4) spare iron hinge pins thrust through his belt; (5) behind him, a massive iron-bound gate leaf hung on huge forged hinges of his own work; the top hinge has a fresh pin, still glowing red-hot. Place: outside the narrow gate of a lone dwarven mountain at dusk, the gate shut behind him, dust and sparks in the air. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the cracks below; the red glow of the hot pin.

jobs.title: Скегги Огнестрел — дворф, физ ДД ловкости, Огонь (c2-09, золото №9, обычная)
jobs.source: roster.js c2-09: «Стрелок гильдейской дружины. Дворфский огнестрел не прощает спешки, и Скегги не спешил ни разу — даже когда было надо»; глава «Последний заряд» (поторопишься — порох вспыхнет у лица; северяне смеялись, что целится дольше, чем они дерутся; «стреляет поздно, зато один раз»; последний заряд — выждал, пока тварь подойдёт вплотную). Свод: огнестрел и заряды делают только в Стоун-Хейме; твари заводятся у ручьёв. Решение агента: миг выстрела в упор — алое пламя Огня и дым из раструба вправо; огнестрел — длинная тяжёлая ручница: восьмигранный ствол тёмного железа в латунных обручах, раструб, резное ложе, латунная полка у казны; все гнёзда патронташа пусты; Скегги (др.-сканд. «бородатый») — великолепная седая борода в косе, заправленная за пояс подальше от полки; ночь, дорога у ручья, факелы ворот вдали. Тварей не рисуем. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-09-skeggi__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-09.jpg
jobs.subject: Subject: Skeggi Firelock, an old dwarf gunner of the guild guard, a marksman of the Fire school. Who he is: a dwarven gun does not forgive haste — hurry, and the powder flashes in your face. In forty years he never once hurried, and the northerners of the caravans laughed that he aimed longer than they fought. At the gate they said: Skeggi shoots late, but only once. Right now he has one charge left and a beast comes straight at him; he has waited until it is so close that missing is impossible. Character: unhurried, calm as stone, with a dry, quiet humour; his face utterly still, one eye narrowed along the barrel, a faint dry calm in the corner of his mouth. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad weathered face with a wide nose; in his seventies, bushy grey brows and a magnificent long grey beard in one thick braid, tucked into his belt, away from the pan. Framing: a close portrait from the belt up — his head, his shoulders, his arms and the gun fill the picture; the bottom edge of the picture cuts him at the belt; his legs and boots are out of the picture. The long barrel runs toward the right edge, and the flash of the shot bursts at the right edge of the picture. Pose, the moment of the shot: the camera is low; he is rock-still, turned toward the right, the heavy gun levelled at his shoulder. He has exactly two arms: his near hand supports the long barrel from beneath; his far hand holds the stock tight to his shoulder, a finger on the trigger. The gun fires at point-blank range: scarlet fire of the Fire school and white smoke burst from the flared muzzle toward the right. Details that tell his story: (1) the gun: a long, heavy dwarven hand-cannon — an eight-sided barrel of dark iron bound with brass bands, a flared muzzle, a heavy carved wooden stock and a small brass pan by the breech; (2) the bandolier across his chest: every loop is empty; (3) the braided beard tucked into his belt; (4) a brass powder flask at his belt; (5) a smouldering slow-match coiled around his wrist. Place: a stony wasteland at night, a dark stream glinting behind him; far away, the torches of the gate of a lone dwarven mountain. Scarlet light of the Fire school from the muzzle and from embers drifting up from below; cold dark night around.

jobs.title: Ньяль Рудный Меняла — дворф, фармер, без стихии (c2-10, золото №10, обычная)
jobs.source: roster.js c2-10: «Менял руду на всё, что везли к воротам, и никогда не брал в долг: долга дворф не признаёт»; глава «Без долга» (равным за равное; в долг предлагали под запись у своих судей — отказывал всем; раз в сезон сверял полки с книгой, и книга сходилась; подручному отдал долю за смену вперёд — это мена, не долг). Свод: чужак входит только со сделкой — мена равным за равное; долга и подарка дворф не признаёт. Решение агента: миг сделки — ближняя рука протягивает вправо, чужаку, кусок руды с металлическими жилами, дальняя лежит на закрытой книге с железной застёжкой (надписей не видно); большие латунные весы, чаши ровно; полки с товаром со всего света; кожаный мешочек на краю прилавка — доля подручного вперёд; лупа на шнуре. Без стихии: свет — фонари и отблески литейных, без цвета школы. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-10-nyal__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-10.jpg
jobs.subject: Subject: Nyal the Ore-Changer, a dwarf trader at the gate of the great dwarven mountain, a gatherer of wealth. Who he is: at the gate everything is exchanged for everything, and he exchanged ore for anything at all — as long as it was equal for equal. People offered him credit — cheap, long, recorded by their judges — and he refused them all: a dwarf recognizes neither debt nor gift. Once a season he checked his shelves against his book, and the book always tallied. Right now a stranger beyond the right edge makes an offer, and he names equal for equal. Character: shrewd, proud and incorruptible — a dwarf who has never owed anyone a thing; one bushy brow raised, a small satisfied smile in his beard, his eyes weighing the stranger. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; in his sixties, a bald head and a long iron-grey beard in a single thick braid bound with copper rings. Pose, the moment of the deal: the camera is low; he leans over his counter toward the right. He has exactly two arms: his near hand is thrust out toward the right, palm up, holding out a heavy lump of raw ore glittering with veins of metal — his offer; his far hand rests flat on a thick closed ledger with an iron clasp. Between them on the counter stand great brass scales, their two pans perfectly level. Details that tell his story: (1) the great brass scales with both pans exactly level — equal for equal; (2) the ledger is closed with its iron clasp, nothing written visible; (3) shelves behind him crowded with goods from all over the world: bales of cloth, jars of oil, bundles of herbs, tools and blades; (4) a small leather pouch set apart at the edge of the counter — his apprentice's share, paid in advance; (5) a jeweller's loupe on a cord around his neck, a heavy leather coat with brass buttons. Place: a trading stall at the great gate of a lone dwarven mountain, where caravans come to exchange: lanterns, crates, pack animals and traders blurred in soft focus, the gate's massive stone arch above. Warm lantern light rises from the counter below and glints on the ore and the brass; the orange glow of the foundries deep inside the gate.
